headline: 42pc of people struggle to meet healthcare costs
description:
Nearly 42 per cent of the country’s population faces financial hardship when paying for medical treatment. In 2022 alone, healthcare expenses pushed 7.2 million people below the poverty line. 

These findings emerged from a study by the Health Economics Unit of the Ministry of Health. The study found that the burden of medical expenses falls most heavily on the poor, with a large share of out-of-pocket spending going towards medicines.

The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Swedish Embassy supported the Health Economics Unit in conducting the study. Its findings were presented at a hotel in the capital on Wednesday. The study used data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics’ (BBS) Household Income and Expenditure Surveys conducted in 2005, 2010, 2016 and 2022.

The aim was to examine how much people spend out of their own pockets when seeking healthcare, which aspects of treatment account for their spending, and how heavily these expenses affect them.

State Minister for Health M A Muhith, the chief guest at the event, said the findings offered a striking illustration of the dire state of the health sector. The BNP was in power at the beginning of the 17-year period from 2005 to 2022, while a “fascist government” was in power for the remaining years. Therefore, he argued, the BNP government could not be held responsible for the picture that emerged from the study.

headline: Why is Padma Barrage necessary, and what are the main challenges
description:
The Padma Barrage is a much-discussed and long-planned project for water management in the southwestern region of Bangladesh. Its potential benefits are numerous: water conservation during the dry season, river revival, irrigation expansion, navigability enhancement, salinity control, increased freshwater flow in the Sundarbans, fish production, and hydroelectricity generation.

headline: Rising tourist numbers put Saint Martin’s Island at risk
description:
To protect Saint Martin’s Island’s natural environment, the daily limit on visitors had been set at an average of 2,000. This year, the government has raised it to 3,500. The period during which tourists can stay overnight has also been extended from two months to four and a half months.

But questions have been raised over whether an updated scientific study has been conducted to determine how much additional pressure the island’s water resources, waste management systems and natural environment can withstand.

Saint Martin’s is an ecologically critical area. More tourists mean greater demand for drinking water, more sewage and rubbish, and heavier foot traffic on the beaches. Environmentalists have questioned whether these pressures were properly considered when the new limit was set.

headline: Police to recruit 4,000 SI directly; special BCS exam to recruit 400–500 ASP
description:
The government will directly recruit 4,000 sub-inspectors (SIs) into Bangladesh Police. The decision came at a meeting of the Secretaries’ Committee on Administrative Development at the Secretariat on Wednesday afternoon. 

The government has amended the Police Regulations of Bengal (PRB) to facilitate direct recruitment to the SI posts.

Under the Police Regulations, 50 per cent of SI posts were previously filled through departmental promotions, while the remaining 50 per cent were filled through direct recruitment. 

Under the existing rules, half of the 4,000 SI posts were also supposed to be filled through departmental promotions. However, the government will not follow that arrangement this time. For the first time, all 4,000 SIs will be recruited directly.
